newsitem.title: USA: Most US stock index futures end higher, off peaks.
newsitem.headline: Most US stock index futures end higher, off peaks.

text.p: Most U.S. stock index futures ended higher but well off session highs as the triple expiration proved to be a non-event, traders and analysts said.
The buy-order imbalance ahead of the close failed to generate much momentum.
At the opening, the buy-order imbalance generated a strong rally. March Standard & Poor's 500s gapped higher for the second day in a row, gaining 11.50 points in the first 15 minutes of trade.
"It got blown way out of proportion," said Kurt Schultz, a floor analyst at Refco Inc.
March S&Ps set a two-week high at 765.00.

The expiration of stock options and other index futures and options contracts failed to drum up any buying interest at the end of the day. December S&P 500s expired at the end of pit trade on Thursday.
In fact, traders and dealers appeared more interested in liquidating long positions.
"I know if I were long I'd be taking profits," Schultz said.
Traders said profit-taking also occurred due to continued declines in the Nasdaq composite.
However, by the end of the session most traders had left ahead of the weekend and the holidays next week. Trade will close at 1215 CST/1815 GMT on Tuesday and will be shut on Wednesday for Christmas.
Fair value is at 6.40 points to cash, with arbitrage buy programs at a premium of 8.00 points and arbitrage sell programs at a premium of 5.50 points.

At the end of pit trade, March S&Ps were up 3.75 points at 757.25, Value Lines were down 0.10 at 686.40, New Composites were up 1.55 at 397.70, Nikkeis were down 210 at 19,610 and Midcap 400s were off 0.75 at 255.05.
